subject: ScaleWave: measurement window exception & rollforward plan for migration
messages:
From: Erin Park <erin.park@scalewave.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.example
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: clarification on p50/p95 windows during migration

Ben —

We're planning a database migration next week (6/24–6/26) that will temporarily change request fan‑out and increase tail latency for a subset of API traffic. Before we schedule the migration, procurement asked us to get the SLO carveout in writing so they can close the change ticket. Can you confirm the exact p50/p95 targets you measure for the hosted API, the measurement epoch/window, and whether Redwood can provide a 72‑hour temporary exception (p95 relaxation) tied to a rollforward plan and audit evidence?

Specifically we need:
- the numeric p50/p95 commitments (post‑SLO vs. contracted)
- how you measure (sampling, epoch length, timezone)
- what evidence you'll provide (traces, per‑token latency histogram)

If easier, we can do a 30 minute call tomorrow.

Thanks —
Erin Park
VP of Engineering, ScaleWave
ops@scalewave.com

Attachment: operational-evidence-request.pdf (1 page stub)

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>
To: Erin Park <erin.park@scalewave.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Date: 2026-06-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: clarification on p50/p95 windows during migration

Erin —

Thanks for the heads up and the attachment. Short answers up front, then a proposed MAP (mutual action plan):

Numeric commitments (hosted API):
- p50: 40–60 ms (typical; measured across all requests for the route)
- p95: 150 ms (contract baseline for the route we discussed)

Measurement details:
- We compute p50/p95 on rolling 1‑hour epochs sampled at 100% for route‑level traffic.
- The rolling window that feeds the SLA check is a 24‑hour aggregation composed of these 1‑hour epochs; SLA adjudication uses the latest 24 discrete 1‑hour buckets (UTC).
- During short maintenance windows we can apply a temporary 72‑hour carveout that excludes the affected IP CIDR/route tag from SLA calculation (requires agreement and an explicit start/end time).

Proposed MAP highlights (attached draft):
- 72‑hour exemption window (2026‑06‑24 08:00 UTC → 2026‑06‑27 08:00 UTC)
- Pre‑migration smoke tests and a post‑migration 4‑hour stabilization period for metric inspection
- Evidence package: per‑route latency histograms, trace samples, and VM/GPU host telemetry for the exemption window
- Rollforward policy: automatic fallback to a lower‑latency model variant if p95 exceeds 300 ms for two consecutive 1‑hour epochs

I'll attach a one‑page MAP and ask Karthik to confirm the technical carveouts. If that looks good I can get Legal to draft a quick addendum via DocuSign.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.example

Attachment: SLO-exception-MAP-v1.pdf (draft)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>, Erin Park <erin.park@scalewave.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.example
Date: 2026-06-22T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: clarification on p50/p95 windows during migration

Erin / Ben —

Technical clarifications from eng: we recommend the following specifics to avoid ambiguity in the exemption clause: 

1) Measurement semantics
- p50 and p95 are computed on per‑request total server processing time (request ingress to final token emission). Client‑side retries are excluded by our proxy filter.
- Sample rate remains 100% for the route but downstream heavy traces are capped at 5% for storage reasons; histograms are still representative due to reservoir sampling.

2) Windowing and aggregation
- SLA uses a sliding 24‑hour window composed of discrete 1‑hour epochs in UTC. Each epoch's p95 must not exceed contractual threshold except for agreed carveouts.
- Temporary exemption: we mark affected epochs as 'transient carveout' in the audit log; those epochs are not counted toward SLA breach checks but are retained for post‑mortem.

3) Rollforward behavior
- On repeated degradation (two consecutive epochs > 300 ms p95), traffic will be routed to a compatible model quantization variant automatically. This reduces latency but may increase token cost by ~8–12%.
- We will suspend the exemption immediately if customer‑visible errors (5xx) spike >0.5% during the window.

I can provide a sanitized example of the hourly histogram export and a sample trace bundle by end of day.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer, Director, Inference Engineering
karthik_iyer@redwood.example

I'll confirm internally but expect a yes. I'll attach our ops ticket and the procurement checklist.

Thanks —
Erin
